newsitem.title: USA: Body of missing U.S. State Dept officer said found.
newsitem.headline: Body of missing U.S. State Dept officer said found.

text.p: The body of a young Foreign Service officer who disappeared Aug. 30 in Shenandoah National Park after coming under suspicion of mishandling missile secrets has been found, WJLA-TV reported Sunday.

The local ABC affiliate said National Park Service investigators were awaiting the results of an autopsy, but believed they found the body of James Schneider, 27, Saturday about 3-1/2 miles from the place where his car was found abandoned.

The investigators told the television station they also found Schneider's personal identification, belongings, a handwritten suicide note, and the handgun he purchased five days before his disappearance.

Schneider, who was about to be posted to Athens, Greece, disappeared after he failed two lie detector tests about his handling of missile secrets while serving as a Naval surface warfare officer aboard the USS Chancellorsville during the Gulf War.
Schneider failed one polygraph test in April 1995 when he applied for a job with the Central Intelligence Agency after ending his tour of duty.
He subsequently applied for and got a job with the State Department, whose own background checks turned up no serious questions about Schneider.
He failed a second polygraph test administered shortly before his disappearance by the FBI, which was called in after the State Department learned of Schneider's failed CIA lie detector test.
The sections he failed focused on whether he had mishandled classified information or had been contacted by foreign agents while he was aboard the ship.
No comment was immediately available from the Washington field office of the FBI. A State Department spokeswoman also declined comment, saying the matter was under police investigation.
Schneider, a resident of Arlington, Va, was last seen Aug. 30 at a restaurant in the national park in Virginia, just days after his assignment to Greece was suspended.

Park rangers found Schneiders' rented car in a parking lot about 10 miles (16 km) from the restaurant. Investigators found Schneider's camping equipment and two boxes of ammunition in the car, but the handgun had been missing until now.
